issue: A free-text turn whose three attempts are rejected ends with one stock line shared by every character ('I can’t help you with that.'): 75 of 756 turns in epoch 0 (10%); judges flagged the identical phrase across characters as scripted and a top frustration in 13 of 18 episodes.
change: Publishing writes four in-voice declines per person that state no fact (code drops digits and names; a model drops any line stating a fact); a rejected turn ends with the person's next decline, rotating; intent 'refuse', not 'clarify'.
guardrails: no new facts (declines are claimless and checked); dialogue AI rate on Death at Vale Manor 97 of 104 (was 90 of 93)

issue: Characters promised later actions that never happen ('I'll come with you to make her show it', 'I'll fetch the ledger') or sent the detective to someone else, who deflected back: judges flagged dead loops of 10-20 actions in 5 of 18 episodes.
change: The character prompt forbids promising a later action or sending the detective elsewhere unless an account or plan says so; the fact-checker rejects such promises explicitly.

status: measured: fails the gate (recommend reverting no-unbacked-promises)
reading: Rejected replies rose by about 23 per game (90% interval 17 to 29) and fallbacks by about 4; solve rate fell 44 points. Only the promise rule makes the fact-checker stricter, so it is the likely cause; the declines change only what is said after a rejection.

reason: Epoch 1 failed the gate. The rule also contradicted the prompt's existing guidance ('if you genuinely do not know, say so simply, and if you can, say who might'), so replies that pointed elsewhere were rejected.
lesson: A rule that widens what the fact-checker rejects must be checked offline for rejection rate, and against the rest of the prompt for contradictions, before play.

variant: A (declines v1, promise rule reverted) vs baseline
hypothesis: Epoch 1's regression came from the promise rule, not from the declines.
mechanism: The rule widened what the fact-checker rejects and contradicted 'say who might'; the declines only change the words after a rejection.
prediction: Rejections per question back to baseline (about 0.6 per turn in play); solved rate not below baseline beyond noise; stock-line replies near 0.
would_refute: Solved rate or rejections still clearly worse than baseline: then the declines themselves (inviting pressing) are harmful.

variant: B (A + chosen account given as written + closing declines v3) vs A
hypothesis: Many rejected free-text turns had a fitting published account; giving it, and closing the subject otherwise, leaves the player with nothing less often and stops pressing.
prediction: Turns ending in a decline fall by about a third (offline 19 -> 13 of 80); same-person turns after a decline fall; longest stall and frustration fall; solved not lower.
would_refute: Declines per game not lower, or solved/fairness lower.

hypothesis: Level-1 testimony hints fail because they name no one (26% helped vs 69% for level 2, which names the person).
prediction: Share of hints that help rises (towards the level-2 rate); hints per solve falls; longest stall falls; solved not lower; challenge may fall slightly (guardrail: not below 3).

conclusion: The promise rule caused the rise in rejections (A is back to the baseline rate). The in-voice declines of version 1 are harmful on their own: players pressed the same person more (+0.72 of the next 5 actions, interval excludes 0) and frustration rose. Superseded by declines v3.

status: concluded: direction as predicted, not significant alone; kept
conclusion: Turns ending in a decline fell by a fifth and pressing fell, as predicted, with intervals that include 0; challenge fell slightly (-0.44). Kept: it removes A's regression (B vs baseline: no metric differs beyond noise).
Hints that helped rose 35 points (interval 19 to 53) and judged fun rose 0.5 (0.1 to 0.9); challenge unchanged.

open: Judged liveliness is 0.33 lower than baseline (interval -0.67 to -0.06); rejections per turn 0.65 against 0.59 (not significant). Watch both next epoch.

variant: A (pushed b41f2fa: bite-sized briefing, contradiction rule, guarded reply only after a fact-checker rejection, line critic sees private knowledge, familiar names, innocent-secret reason, victim pronoun) vs baseline (epoch 2C code, pre-fix case data); fresh held-out cases heldout3, 3 profiles x 3 seeds = 27 pairs

hypotheses.briefing: A briefing that names one person and one place gets players to their first evidence sooner. Primary: first_progress lower.
hypotheses.contradictions: Where a sighting broke a lie without counting (The Quarter-Past Watch), fewer accusations are refused with 'evidence rules out everyone'. Primary: refused_inconsistent lower; wrong_accusations not higher.
hypotheses.guarded: Fewer secretive replies after a refused name: pressing_after_decline lower.

side_effects: The line critic may refuse more meeting lines: witnessed_village_per_hour and judged liveliness may fall (guardrail: liveliness not lower beyond noise).
would_refute: first_progress not lower, or refused_inconsistent not lower on The Quarter-Past Watch.

variant: C (A + hints name the action that actually gives the account) vs A; heldout3, 27 pairs
hypothesis: Testimony hints often quote the evening question, which gives a different account (scripted check: 13 of 36 followed hints in 13 cases did not give their account; after the change 0 of 23); players then stall or press with free text.
secondary: longest_stall lower; solved not lower; hint_no_help problem records fewer
side_effects: Hints may solve more of the case for the player: judged challenge may fall (guardrail: not below 3.5 on average).
note: Change B (spoken times by value) is a correctness fix whose offline replay showed no fewer time rejections (11 vs 11 of 80 questions); it is kept out of this arm.

variant: D (C + after code checks alone, the third attempt is a plain in-character 'nothing to tell') vs C; heldout3, 27 pairs
observation: Arm A raised declines from 5.2% to 7.0% of character turns (+1.15 per game, interval 0.33 to 2.0). Declines after code-check failures alone rose 19 -> 31, and 'repeated_clarify' failures among declines 32 -> 59: without the guarded third attempt, the free retry repeats the refused clarifying question.
secondary: character_fallbacks lower; pressed_after_decline not higher; character_quality not lower

status: concluded: not supported as predicted; kept as correctness fixes
result: 27 pairs, fresh held-out cases: fairness +0.41 [0.0, 0.85]; declines +1.15 [0.33, 2.0] (the free third retry repeats a refused clarifying question); first progress +0.33 actions; refused 'rules out everyone' unchanged (rare in agent play).

status: concluded: refuted in play; kept as a correctness fix
result: hints that helped 0.00 [-0.08, 0.07] vs A. The scripted check's failure (13 of 36 followed hints) is removed, but agents seldom follow a hint exactly enough to meet it.

23 pairs: declines -0.56 and fallbacks -0.61 (not significant) but pressing after a decline +0.75 [0.20, 1.38] and village events seen -0.12: the epoch-1 pattern again (a softer refusal invites pressing).
